crates.name: uor-r4-discrete
crates.role: Active M1 model path: exact SpiralCore/FBS discrete learning, shared integer vector writer, CUDA driver and qualification/admission instruments (rows, rows-K, BVG-K, prime-zeta, address-cells).
crates.notes: uor-r4-core is a BUILD-dependency only (build.rs imports spiralcore_operator: cl06_bivectors, cl06_finite_composition_table, SignedMatrix8 to emit exact 64-state geometry tables into OUT_DIR/geometry.rs); it is not in the runtime graph. Runtime deps are only serde, serde_json, sha2 and optional cudarc =0.19.10 (feature cuda, default off). Without feature cuda, build.rs still runs the PTX-admission self-test and generates geometry but invokes no nvcc. With feature cuda it needs UOR_NVCC_ARCH=compute_<n> explicitly (no default) and nvcc. Several src files are include_bytes!/include_str! consumers of docs/labs evidence JSON and docs/harness/prep markdown (attention_learning.rs), so the crate is coupled to docs paths. Also path-depended on by out-of-workspace lab instruments under docs/labs/*/instrument (5 of the 12 standalone Cargo projects under docs/labs name it).

crates.name: uor-r4-core
crates.role: Original 'R4 engine': zeta/Hopf/prime math, historical native_geometric engine, transformerless compiler/runtime pieces, ~50 research binaries; the only live piece for the M1 path is spiralcore_operator.rs (1381 lines).
bins: ~50 auto-discovered src/bin/* (e.g. train-native-prose, train-lowbit-chat, integrated-attention*, addressed-attention-*, geometric-realtext-*, query-read, relational-reader, r4-policy-check, prior-learning-*, readout-diagnostic)
crates.notes: Status is mixed: 'active-model' only because uor-r4-discrete build-depends on it (and CI runs r4-policy-check and native_geometric tests from it). By far the largest crate; most of its 347k lines (native_geometric/, transformerless/, learned_reference/, semantic/, helm_d_r4_attention, many *_attention.rs) are historical or frozen Sept-era evidence per AGENTS.md. notes:
WORKSPACE SHAPE. Cargo.toml members: 25 crates + xtask + tools/lab-runner (27 entries) plus the root package uor-r4-wasm-router. default-members = root, core, graph-format, router, proof-model, graph-runtime. One crate, uor-r4-model-source, is NOT in members but is an implicit workspace member as a path dependency (29 packages in the graph: 27 members + root + model-source). exclude: uor_standards, graph-format/fuzz, research, third_party/{arrayref,candle-*,cudarc,float8,uor-addr}. Rust toolchain pinned 1.97.1. [patch.crates-io] redirects candle-core/nn/kernels, cudarc, float8, arrayref to third_party and uor-foundation(-sdk) to a pinned UOR-Framework git rev.

ACTIVE M1 PATH. Needs only uor-r4-discrete, which needs at build time uor-r4-core (-> integer, tokenizer, source-interface, vendored uor-addr). Nothing else in the workspace is needed: not training, graph-*, api, router, lut, simd, object-store, harness, root package. Runtime crate deps are serde, serde_json, sha2 and optional cudarc. The 347k-line core compiled solely to obtain 1381 lines of spiralcore_operator.rs is the biggest structural wart; extracting that module would shrink the active model's build closure by ~99 percent of core. discrete is 33,291 lines and itself carries many qualification instruments (attention_*, bvgk_*, rows_*, rowsk_*, flock_*, relation_*, redirect_admission, completion*) that are research-line-specific and could be moved under a qualification/ sub-area.

CUDA INVENTORY. Four nvcc-driven build scripts: discrete (6 modules: ordinary 12 entries, decomposition, baseline-reuse, rows, rows-K, BVG-K; each gets nvcc -ptx, PTX admission, then nvcc -cubin --ptxas-options=-v with resource report), training (3 PTX modules), third_party/candle-kernels (9 modules, via training cuda feature), plus the out-of-tree lab instrument. NVRTC is banned (13 Oct 2026); all compilation is ahead of time. No GitHub workflow mentions nvcc or CUDA, so CUDA code is never built in CI (CI cargo check --workspace runs without the cuda feature); qualification runs on pods. Other build.rs files (graph-cli, harness) are not CUDA: graph-cli records PROFILE/OPT_LEVEL, harness records build time.

PTX ADMISSION AUDIT (crates/uor-r4-discrete/build.rs). admit_ptx_inventory(ptx, inventory) lexes the emitted PTX text line by line (comments after // stripped, split on non-alphanumeric/underscore/dot) and rejects the build if any token has a dot-component in {f16,f16x2,f32,f64,bf16,bf16x2,tf32,e4m3,e5m2,mma,wmma,wgmma,tcgen05,tensor,tensormap} or starts with ex2.approx: i.e. no floating-point types, tensor-core/matrix instructions or approximate-exp. Integer multiplies are explicitly allowed (index products). It also parses .entry declarations and requires the entry set to EXACTLY equal the declared inventory (missing or unexpected or duplicate entries fail; unterminated entry fails). The inspected object is the emitted PTX, not the CUDA source spelling. ptx_admission_self_test() runs at every build (even without the cuda feature): it accepts a clean module (floats inside comments are fine, mul.lo.u32 allowed) and requires rejection of add.f32, .reg .bf16, mma.sync, ex2.approx, an unexpected entry, a duplicate entry, and missing entries. After admission, the exact admitted PTX (not re-compiled source) is assembled with nvcc -cubin --ptxas-options=-v --gpu-code=sm_NN for each of six labels (ordinary, decomposition, baseline-reuse, rows, rowsk, bvgk); the build fails if the cubin is not a nonempty ELF or the resource report is empty. cuda-image-target.txt records the sm target. Each later generated module (rows, rowsk, bvgk) is its own source, PTX and cubin, leaving earlier images byte-for-byte unchanged. geometry_source() also emits exact tables from core: AXES[512], COMPOSE[4096], INVERSE[64], ROOTS[16][8], BFS[256], BRANCH[48], GENERATORS[15], with BFS reachability asserted over all 64 frames and 16 roots and operator/composition kappa constants. Note the training crate has NO equivalent PTX admission (float is legal there under D37) and uses precision flags instead. The lab instrument docs/labs/admission-rank-fixture-runner-2026-10-15/instrument/build.rs holds a divergent copy of admit_ptx with the 12-entry inventory only.

TESTS. Test counts are #[test] attribute counts in src/ and tests/ (rough, include ignored): core 1700, training 1208, harness 580, integer 519, root 499, api 255, graph-certify 255, graph-compiler 329, model-source 222, discrete 212, graph-format 187, graph-cli 157, lab-runner 122, workbench 65, object-store 61, graph-runtime 53, router 43, repo-conformance 43, xtask 38, proof-model 28, tokenizer 22, repo-model 9, claim-wording 13, recon-dag 13, pod-provider 8, simd 7, naf 6, lut 5, source-interface 0. LoC are raw line counts of src/**/*.rs (tests/ and examples/ excluded), so the figures for core and training include all bin/ files even where cargo does not build them. Sum of crate src is about 0.9 million lines of Rust.

CI COVERAGE (.github/workflows). ci.yml runs claim-wording, fmt, cargo check --workspace --all-targets, cargo test --workspace --lib, clippy -D warnings all-features, nextest, bdd, doc tests, and a native-geometric job (r4-policy-check, native_geometric lib tests, windowed_geometric_context, native_geometric_allocations, `--bin r4 native_geometric_`). harness.yml covers only uor-r4-harness; formal_verification.yml covers uor-r4-proof-model (tests + Kani); relative-query-check.yml; deploy.yml (wasm-pack Pages); release.yml (cargo build --release --locked). So every workspace member is compile-checked but few have dedicated test jobs, and the active uor-r4-discrete has none (only compile check and lib tests via the workspace run, with no cuda feature).

OUT-OF-WORKSPACE CODE. About 12 standalone Cargo projects under docs/labs/*/{instrument,harness,tests,report-tool,receipt-audit,metadata-audit,scoring-audit} are lab instruments with their own Cargo.lock; some path-depend on uor-r4-discrete and cudarc. Also uor_standards/ (UOR-Framework, prism, uor-addr submodule-style checkouts excluded from workspace), research/ (excluded), third_party/helm-d-reference. Python remains in scripts/*.py (dozens), tools/uor-knowledge, tools/r4-softmax-trainer, tools/lab-host despite the Rust-first rule (D27); scripts/ also holds check_no_softmax.py / check_no_matmul.py (retired in favor of uor-harness ratchet).

OBSERVATIONS FOR THE REORG. (1) Three de-facto products share one workspace: the active M1 discrete model (discrete+core), the old R4G1/transformerless stack (graph-*, api, proof-model, router, model-source, root r4/wasm), and tooling/ops (harness, lab-runner, xtask, pod-provider, repo-*). (2) SpiralCore-as-own-project candidates in code: spiralcore_operator.rs and spiralcore_fbs.rs live inside core/discrete/training rather than a spiralcore crate; uor-r4-recon-dag and parts of uor-r4-object-store are in the same family. (3) Webclient lives in the root package (wasm cdylib, Pages studio via deploy.yml) and the desktop client does not exist yet: no crate named for it. (4) model-source is a transformer teacher that graph-compiler, graph-certify, graph-cli and api all depend on, so the whole R4G1 stack drags in the comparator. (5) uor-r4-model-source dev-depends on uor-r4-api while api depends on model-source (dev-dep cycle allowed by cargo). (6) tools/lab-host has a __pycache__ directory in the working tree; verify whether it is tracked.
